Vladyslav Yatsenko is a Director of Revolut Ltd (appointed 11 August 2017), co-founder & CTO of Revolut; British nationality.
Caroline Louise Britton is a Director of Revolut Ltd (appointed 8 March 2019); British nationality.

Dan Teodosiu is a Director of Revolut Ltd (appointed 27 November 2023); Austrian nationality.
Siddhartha Jajodia is a Director of Revolut Ltd (appointed 9 July 2026); American nationality.

Revolut Group Holdings Ltd is the active person with significant control of Revolut Ltd, holding 75% or more of shares and voting rights, notified 29 April 2022.
Nikolay Storonsky was a former PSC of Revolut Ltd (more than 25% but not more than 50% of shares) and ceased 29 April 2022 when the parent took over.

PEP screening: Nikolay Storonsky (Revolut co-founder & CEO) is not designated a PEP on OpenSanctions, but has a PEP-relevant family association: his father Nikolay Mironovich Storonsky was deputy general director for science at Gazprom Promgaz (1999–2019) and became its CEO in December 2019.
Nikolay Storonsky was born in Russia (Dolgoprudny) and renounced Russian citizenship in 2022.

OFAC SDN screening (via OpenSanctions): no match for Revolut Ltd (08804411) and its owners; only Revolut Payments Australia Pty Ltd, a group company with no sanctions designations, appears in name search.
UK OFSI/UK Sanctions List screening (via OpenSanctions): no match for Revolut Ltd, Revolut Group Holdings Ltd and Nikolay Storonsky.
EU consolidated sanctions list screening: no match for Nikolay Storonsky; flagged only as 'person of interest' with a 'sanction-linked' topic annotation, not a designation.

Adverse media (2025-04-08): Lithuania's central bank fined Revolut EUR 3.5m, its largest ever, for AML monitoring shortcomings; the fine was set against Revolut Holdings Europe revenues; Revolut settled with the Bank of Lithuania and said no confirmed money laundering was identified.

Adverse media (2023-10-02): The UK FCA investigated Revolut for allegedly allowing withdrawals from NCA-flagged suspicious accounts; FT estimated £1.7m released in July–August 2023 while Revolut said £500,000; no public enforcement outcome found as of 2026-10-20.

Adverse media (2023-03-01): Auditor BDO flagged it could not verify £477m of Revolut Ltd's £636m 2021 revenues; FRC earlier called the 2020 audit 'inadequate'; the issue delayed Revolut's UK banking licence and CFO Mikko Salovaara left in May 2023.

Adverse media (2026-07-10): Lithuania's FNTT said Revolut accounts for ~80% of suspicious transaction reports in Lithuania (about 80,000 of ~100,000), mostly potential fraud; Revolut attributed this to its scale and AI monitoring; no enforcement action announced.

Adverse media (2025-12): FT reported Revolut did not inform UK regulators in advance of a Companies House filing listing CEO Nikolay Storonsky as a UAE resident; the filing was later amended as an 'administrative error'.
Adverse media (2025-11): Revolut was criticised for freezing accounts of Russian expatriates in Europe, which it said was to comply with EU sanctions against Russia.
Revolut Bank UK Ltd received PRA approval in March 2026 to launch as a fully licensed UK bank after restrictions were lifted (mitigating finding); customers migrating in phased batches during 2026.
Revolut Ltd KYC risk rating is medium, driven by adverse regulatory history rather than registration or sanctions risk.
Revolut Group Holdings Ltd (registry number 12743269) is the ultimate parent and sole active PSC of Revolut Ltd.
Revolut Bank UK Ltd (formerly Revolut Newco UK Ltd, renamed effective 2026-03-12; registry number 12871051) is a group subsidiary of Revolut and a newly licensed UK bank.
Revolut Trading Ltd (registry number 11567840, UK, incorporated 2018-09-13) is a Revolut group subsidiary.
Revolut Holdings International Ltd (registry number 12734772, UK, incorporated 2020-07-10) is a Revolut group holding company.

PEP-related finding: Revolut founder/controller Nikolay Storonskiy has potential close-family PEP exposure (not a confirmed personal PEP designation); reporting dated 2022-10-29 identifies his father, Nikolay Storonsky Sr, as director general of Kremlin-controlled Gazprom Promgaz and subject to Ukrainian sanctions. The father is a different person; this is not an OFAC, UK or EU designation of the founder.

Adverse media (2019-04-01, high severity): BBC reported whistleblower allegations about AML controls at Revolut's UK e-money business and temporary disabling of an automatic transaction-halting mechanism for potential sanctions matches; FCA said its enquiries resulted in requirements for specific actions; Revolut disputed allegations about management and compliance. No money laundering or sanctions evasion finding established.

Adverse media (2023-09-30, high severity): Reporting described FCA/NCA scrutiny of Revolut's UK e-money operation over alleged releases of up to £1.7m from accounts flagged as suspicious; reported review and allegations, not an adjudicated breach; later outcome not established.

Adverse media (2024-06-04, medium severity): In Larsson v Revolut Limited, a fraud victim brought contract, negligence and dishonest assistance claims against Revolut; contract and tort claims were struck out and the dishonest-assistance claim could proceed only if properly repleaded. Interlocutory judgment, not a finding of dishonesty or final liability.

Adverse media (2024-06-12, medium severity): In Terna Energy Trading doo v Revolut Ltd, an unjust-enrichment claim following a fraudulent payment, the court dismissed Revolut's summary-judgment/strike-out application and required a trial; permission to appeal was subsequently granted; final disposition unverified.

Adverse media (2024-10-14, high severity): BBC Panorama reported customer allegations of account-security failures and disputed reimbursement involving Revolut's UK e-money business; not a regulatory fine or judicial finding of fraud.

Adverse media (2025-10, medium severity): BBC reported an ombudsman decided in favour of a business-account scam victim and Revolut reimbursed the loss and paid compensation; no broader enforcement finding established.
